quests.question: One of the most striking aspects of the report ___ the lack of transparency.
quests.hint: The subject is 'one' (singular) - 'of the most striking aspects' is a modifier.
quests.explanation: The subject is 'one', which is always singular. 'Of the most striking aspects of the report' is a modifier. 'One of the most striking aspects is the lack of transparency'.

quests.question: Some of the most striking aspects of the report ___ the lack of transparency.
quests.hint: The subject is 'some of the most striking aspects' (plural) - verb agrees with 'aspects'.
quests.explanation: 'Some of the most striking aspects' is the subject. 'Aspects' is plural, so the verb is 'are'. Contrast with 'one of the aspects is'.

quests.question: The growth of both domestic and international markets ___ accelerating.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the growth' (singular) - all other words are modifiers.
quests.explanation: 'The growth' is the singular subject. 'Of both domestic and international markets' is a prepositional modifier. 'The growth is accelerating'.

quests.question: What struck most observers ___ the scale of the response.
quests.hint: A clause beginning with 'what' acts as a single noun when it is the subject.
quests.explanation: The subject 'what struck most observers' is a noun clause acting as a singular unit. 'What struck most observers was the scale of the response'.

quests.question: What struck most observers ___ the speed and scale of the response.
quests.hint: The subject is the 'what' clause - a singular noun clause - not the complement after the verb.
quests.explanation: Even when the complement ('the speed and scale') is plural, the subject 'what struck most observers' is still a singular noun clause. 'What struck observers was the speed and scale'.

quests.question: The findings, none of which ___ unexpected, have been published.
quests.hint: 'None of which' points back to 'the findings' - how many findings were there?
quests.explanation: 'None of which' refers to 'the findings', which is plural. The verb inside the relative clause must also be plural: 'none of which were unexpected'.

quests.question: The proposals, several of which ___ rejected, are being revised.
quests.hint: 'Several of which' refers back to 'the proposals' - plural or singular?
quests.explanation: 'Several of which' refers to 'the proposals', which is plural. The verb inside the relative clause matches the plural: 'several of which were rejected'.

quests.question: The applicants, one of whom ___ offered the position, are waiting.
quests.hint: 'One of whom' refers to one singular person - verb inside clause is singular.
quests.explanation: 'One of whom' refers to a single person from the group of applicants. The verb inside the relative clause is 'was': 'one of whom was offered the position'.

quests.question: The students, most of whom ___ from abroad, adjusted quickly.
quests.hint: 'Most of whom' refers to 'the students' (plural) - verb inside clause agrees.
quests.explanation: 'Most of whom' refers to 'the students', which is plural. The verb inside the relative clause is 'were': 'most of whom were from abroad'.

quests.question: Neither the report nor the analysis ___ been peer-reviewed.
quests.hint: The nearer subject is 'the analysis' - what is its number?
quests.explanation: The verb agrees with the subject nearest to it. 'The analysis' is singular, so 'has been peer-reviewed' is correct. The report comes first but the analysis is closer to the verb.

quests.question: Neither the analysis nor the reports ___ been peer-reviewed.
quests.hint: The subject immediately before the verb gap is 'the reports' - singular or plural?
quests.explanation: The subject nearest to the verb is 'the reports', which is plural. With 'neither…nor', the verb agrees with this nearer subject: 'have been peer-reviewed'.

quests.question: Both the approach and the methodology ___ thoroughly evaluated.
quests.hint: When you see 'both…and', the resulting compound subject always needs a plural verb.
quests.explanation: 'Both…and' combines two items into a plural compound subject. 'Both the approach and the methodology were thoroughly evaluated' - plural verb is required.

quests.question: The way the new systems interact with existing infrastructure ___ under review.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the way' (singular) - the embedded clause is a modifier.
quests.explanation: 'The way' is the singular subject; 'the new systems interact with existing infrastructure' is a clause that modifies 'the way'. 'The way is under review'.

quests.question: The ways in which new systems interact with existing infrastructure ___ under review.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the ways' (plural) - the prepositional phrase is a modifier.
quests.explanation: 'The ways' is the plural subject; 'in which new systems interact with existing infrastructure' is a modifier. 'The ways are under review'.

quests.question: The significance of these findings ___ yet to be fully understood.
quests.hint: 'The significance' is singular - 'of these findings' is a modifier.
quests.explanation: 'The significance' is the singular subject; 'of these findings' modifies it. 'The significance is yet to be fully understood'.

quests.question: Each of the documents submitted for review ___ been carefully scrutinised.
quests.hint: 'Each of' is always singular - even with a plural noun following it.
quests.explanation: 'Each of' is always singular, regardless of the noun that follows. 'Each of the documents has been scrutinised' - not 'have'.

quests.question: All of the documents submitted for review ___ been carefully scrutinised.
quests.hint: 'All of' with a plural countable noun takes a plural verb.
quests.explanation: 'All of the documents' takes a plural verb because 'documents' is countable and plural. 'All of the documents have been scrutinised'.

quests.question: Either the senior researcher or the junior researchers ___ responsible for this.
quests.hint: The subject immediately before the blank is 'the junior researchers' - singular or plural?
quests.explanation: The nearest subject to the verb is 'the junior researchers', which is plural. With 'either…or', the verb agrees with this nearer subject: 'are responsible'.

quests.question: Either the junior researchers or the senior researcher ___ responsible for this.
quests.hint: The subject immediately before the blank is 'the senior researcher' - singular or plural?
quests.explanation: The nearest subject to the verb is 'the senior researcher', which is singular. With 'either…or', the verb agrees with this nearer subject: 'is responsible'.

quests.question: The decision, together with its rationale, ___ communicated to all stakeholders.
quests.hint: The main subject is 'the decision' (singular) - 'together with its rationale' is parenthetical.
quests.explanation: 'Together with its rationale' is a parenthetical addition. The main subject is 'the decision', which is singular: 'was communicated to all stakeholders'.

quests.question: The decisions, together with their rationale, ___ communicated to all stakeholders.
quests.hint: The main subject is 'the decisions' (plural) - 'together with their rationale' is parenthetical.
quests.explanation: 'Together with their rationale' is parenthetical. The main subject is 'the decisions', which is plural: 'were communicated to all stakeholders'.

quests.question: To succeed in a competitive market ___ the primary goal of every new business.
quests.hint: An infinitive phrase starting with 'to' acts as a single subject - singular or plural?
quests.explanation: An infinitive phrase ('to succeed in a competitive market') acting as subject is always treated as singular. 'To succeed is the primary goal' - not 'are the primary goal'.

quests.question: Achieving consistent results across all departments ___ the company's main challenge.
quests.hint: The subject here is an activity (a gerund phrase) - how do gerund subjects behave?
quests.explanation: A gerund phrase functioning as the subject is always treated as a single unit. 'Achieving consistent results across all departments is the company's main challenge'.

quests.question: The ability of individuals to adapt quickly ___ what distinguishes high performers.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the ability' (singular) - all other words are modifiers.
quests.explanation: 'The ability' is the singular subject. 'Of individuals to adapt quickly' is a modifier telling us what kind of ability. 'The ability is what distinguishes high performers'.

quests.question: The combination of skills and experience she brings ___ unique.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the combination' (singular) - 'of skills and experience' is a modifier.
quests.explanation: 'The combination' is the singular subject; 'of skills and experience she brings' is a modifier. 'The combination is unique'.

quests.question: The skills and experience she brings ___ unique.
quests.hint: 'Skills and experience' joined by 'and' form a plural compound subject.
quests.explanation: Now 'skills and experience' is the compound subject joined by 'and', making it plural. 'The skills and experience she brings are unique'.

quests.question: The rate at which these changes ___ occurring has accelerated.
quests.hint: Inside the relative clause, 'which' refers to 'these changes' (plural).
quests.explanation: 'Which' refers to 'these changes', which is plural. The verb inside the relative clause is 'are': 'at which these changes are occurring'.

quests.question: The pace at which new technologies ___ being developed is extraordinary.
quests.hint: Inside the relative clause, 'which' refers to 'new technologies' (plural).
quests.explanation: 'Which' in the relative clause refers to 'new technologies', which is plural. The verb inside the clause is 'are': 'at which new technologies are being developed'.

quests.question: The speed at which the new technology ___ being adopted is extraordinary.
quests.hint: Inside the relative clause, 'which' refers to 'the new technology' (singular).
quests.explanation: 'Which' refers to 'the new technology', which is singular. The verb inside the relative clause is 'is': 'at which the new technology is being adopted'.

quests.question: The vast majority of the work involved in this project ___ been completed.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the vast majority of the work' - 'work' is uncountable, so the verb is singular.
quests.explanation: 'Work' is uncountable. When 'the majority of' is followed by an uncountable noun, the verb is singular: 'the vast majority of the work has been completed'.
